No material flaw was identified. Confidence remains limited by an involved AI workflow and no formal proof verification.

rigor.basis: Explicit hypotheses, fixed finite bootstrap indices, all-sector analysis and stationary-mean-zero normalization support the stated results. Dense notation and local symbol reuse reduce accessibility, but no invalid step was found.

novelty.basis: Several exact model-specific statements are plausible novelty candidates. Primary checks confirm classical ingredients and appropriate attribution; bounded reading does not establish global priority.

significance.basis: The paper controls broad code-supported families and confines possible anomalous modes to a high block and rare high-u sets. The unrestricted gap and critical endpoint remain open, and no physical Yang-Mills consequence is proved.

reproducibility.basis: Exact source/PDF hashes, complete analytic proofs, full diagnostics and all page renders are retained. Two fresh checkouts produced identical PDFs on one runner/toolchain. This verifies document production, not independent formal or numerical checking of the mathematics.

summary: First assessment of the exact 16-page window-revision PDF: accept as a scoped mathematical working paper. The amplitude-uniform full-chain code theorem and dimension-free low-to-all spectral window are substantive; no material mathematical objection was identified. The actual high block, unrestricted stationary gap and critical moment remain uncontrolled. Importance 4.00 means strong on the AIRR comparison scale, not a probability or Yang-Mills progress fraction. All 16 rendered pages were inspected; production records and matching PDF hashes support the successful authorized run. This reviewer participated in prior source audits and inherited shared context; review is not blind, human, provider-independent or organizationally independent. Exact backend/version and effort are unattested. No previous PDF score is inherited and later E-L results are excluded. Metadata notice: v2 is author-proposed and version_id is LOCAL PROVISIONAL assessment packaging, not an AIRR-issued identifier or publication receipt; reconcile the actual revision record before external submission while retaining this original report and its findings.
strengths: Actual Doob normalization and conjugate spectral representations are explicit; quotient-only control is not mistaken for full-chain control.
The code-supported theorem controls every coset uniformly over positive potential amplitudes and includes a valid strict representation-separation witness.
A fixed finite bootstrap crosses 1+rho and yields a whole-operator low-degree estimate without a dimension factor.
The high-block comparison and fixed-margin eigenfunction localization retain the correct Perron and stationary-mean-zero conditions.
Exact-cap failure, generic tail obstruction and unresolved endpoints are clearly separated from an admissible collapsing-gap counterexample.
All 16 pages are readable, and raw hashes confirm matching PDFs from two fresh checkouts and the delivered artifact.
weaknesses: Priority of the specific model-dependent statements is not established by the bounded primary-literature check.
The manuscript is dense and reuses several symbols locally; a notation table would improve accessibility.
Constants are for fixed parameters and may deteriorate near rho endpoints; no uniform endpoint or practical finite-size conclusion follows.
The original full-class gap question and the critical weighting moment remain open; the high-block reduction does not bound the high block.
Assessment has shared context and prior reviewer involvement, and there is no human peer review or proof-assistant verification.
Document reproduction used the same runner/toolchain, and two harmless overfull-line warnings remain in the log.
strong_novelty_candidates: The normalized exact numerical-cap counterexample for stationary-to-weighting moment transfer, subject to further priority checking.
The explicit floor-derived reciprocal bootstrap and finite crossing sufficient for a low-to-all spectral window, subject to further prior-art comparison.
Amplitude-uniform all-coset bounds for actual Boolean Doob potentials supported on code algebras, beyond quotient-only spectral control.
The combined whole-operator window, actual high-block reduction and fixed-margin stationary localization consequences under the original matching hypotheses.
